text: AWS Lake Formation — permissions that understand databases, tables, and columns, layered on top of IAM and the Glue Data Catalog.
The named resource method grants permissions by picking a specific database and table directly, as opposed to granting against an LF-Tag expression.

Lake Formation has its own permission vocabulary — Alter, Insert, Drop, Delete, Select, Describe. And Grantable permissions are tracked separately: using a permission and being able to re-grant it to someone else are two different checkboxes.
Choosing Select unlocks data permissions — all data access by default, or narrowed to specific columns, or down to cell-level filters combining column and row rules.
Everything the console wizard collects maps onto a real GRANT statement — select columns, which table, which role.
